title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-olivia-park
content:
PR: refactor-batching-kv-cache (#482)
Author: @morgan-lee
Summary: attempt to simplify KV cache interaction layer and decouple batching logic from cache eviction. Main change: introduce CacheView interface + move batching heuristics into Batcher class.

Quick notes / first-pass impressions:
- High level looks reasonable. Breaking out Batcher is good for testability.
- Need stronger comments around concurrency model for CacheView (who owns locks?).
- Some naming nits (CacheView vs CacheWindow) — CacheView feels imprecise, maybe CacheWindow/ShardView?

Checklist (run through before approving):
- [ ] unit tests for CacheView concurrency (multi-threaded access)
- [ ] integration tests for end-to-end batching under load (see perf test plan INF-3397)
- [ ] perf numbers: before/after token throughput (p95 latency) for 1k reqs baseline
- [ ] ensure no object allocation hot path in Batcher.add() (avoid alloc per token)
- [ ] logging: ensure we don't log per-token in hot path (some debug logs present)
- [ ] docs: update internal cache contract doc + add diagram for Batcher lifecycle

Detailed concerns / suggestions:
1) Concurrency model (big one)
- The new CacheView exposes getPrefix(), evictRange(), and snapshot(). Thread-safety contract is not documented. Is CacheView expected to be lock-free read-mostly with compare-and-swap eviction? If not, who holds the write lock during eviction?
- Suggestion: add a short comment block at interface level: "thread-safety: readers may call getPrefix concurrently; evictRange must be called under writeLock obtained via CacheCoordinator" (or provide an explicit lock API).

2) Batcher.add() micro-allocs
- Implementation builds a small metadata struct per token. In hot path (GPT- style batching), this will allocate per-token and GC churn could be significant.
- Suggest pre-allocating a reusable token-bucket or using object pools (we have an internal BytesPool + MutableSlice pool — consider reusing).
- If we can't pool yet, at least benchmark with JMH-ish harness and record allocation rate.

3) Eviction semantics + partial hits
- Current evictRange uses exclusive end indexes; code in serving loop assumes evictRange returns number of removed tokens. There's an edge-case where partial KV hits + concurrent append may cause off-by-one and leave stale entries.
- Tests should simulate concurrent append+evict with interleaving. Add a test with randomized schedule to catch races.

4) Metrics and tracing
- Batcher should emit per-batch timing and batch_size histograms. There's a metrics TODO but no concrete metric names. Propose: batcher.batch_size, batcher.queue_time_ms, batcher.process_time_ms.
- Add trace spans: batcher.enqueued / batcher.process. Help debugging of tail latency.

5) API surface + internal vs external
- CacheView currently exposes snapshot() which returns a pointer to an internal buffer. Risk: callers might hold reference and mutate or use after eviction. Either return an immutable copy or provide explicit lifetime/ownership docs.

6) Tests missing for error paths
- When KV backend returns ErrOutOfMemory / ErrUnavailable, Batcher currently retries with backoff but no circuit breaker. Need to verify behavior under sustained backend failures (avoid infinite retry loops causing queue growth).

Small code nits (line refs from diff):
- L72: rename function => capture intent (isBlockingAppend?)
- L134: TODO remove debug println (leftover)
- L198: magic number 64 -> make config MAX_BATCH_SIZE default const
- L220: prefer use of Optional instead of null for MaybeKVResponse

Refactor suggestions (non-blocking but nice-to-have):
- Move batching policy strategy into a pluggable strategy impl (LatencyFirst / ThroughputFirst). Makes experiments easier and isolates heuristics.
- Consider splitting CacheView into ReadOnlyCacheView + MutableCacheView to make ownership explicit.
- Add lightweight adapter that maps old cache calls to new interface to ease rollout (can be removed post-rollout).

Follow-ups / action items if we merge:
- Follow-up ticket to add benchmark harness + perf dashboard (INF-34xx)
- Doc PR to update cache contract + diagram (assign to @avery-kim)
- Add canary rollout plan: enable for 10% of traffic on dedicated cluster for 48h, monitor p95 latency and error rate.

Questions for author / to discuss in review:
- Why was snapshot() chosen to return internal buffer vs copy? Are we avoiding copies for perf? If so, can we at least return a read-only view object with explicit invalidation?
- Any metrics from local benchmark runs (I don't see numbers in PR description)?
- Is there an intended migration plan for existing persisted cache on-disk format? Will new CacheView be compatible or require migration?

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- thread-safety documented + tests for concurrent access
- perf numbers attached to PR showing no regressions (target <= 5% p95 latency regression, preferably improvement)
- no per-token allocs in hot path or documented mitigation (pooling)
- graceful error handling with circuit breaker/backoff
- add minimal metrics + trace spans

Notes to self (todo):
- run perf harness locally: ./tools/loadtest --suite=batcher --qps=500 --concurrency=64
- write multithreaded unit that fuzzes append+evict (use gtest/thread sanitizer)
- ping @samira for KV backend semantics (she owns persistence layer)

Random fragments / brain-dump:
- think about cache sharding key (sessionId % N) vs range-based shards — range shards easier for eviction but harder to reshard. note: resharding is painful.
- maybe add soft-ttl for inactive sessions to reduce memory footprint.
- tie cache eviction events to metrics and auto-trigger compaction in background.

OK that's enough for now. Will re-run tests after author pushes next iteration.

-- Olivia
